title: Archives and scheduled work
subtitle: Package a directory, verify the archive, and schedule a repeatable job without creating a silent failure.
objectives: Create and inspect a compressed tar archive
Restore an archive into a clean directory
Read and write cron schedule fields
Install and inspect a user crontab
Decide when a systemd timer is a better choice than cron

ex200.evidence: Compare supervision, logs, and Persistent behavior.

versionNotes: RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 both use cronie and the same five-field user crontab format. The crond service is enabled by default on standard installations.
systemd timers are preferred for system-level jobs with dependencies or journal requirements. RHEL 10 keeps both interfaces; do not assume cron has been removed.

commands.desc: Create a gzip-compressed archive of one directory.
Extract into a specific, clean directory.
Show the current user’s cron entries.
Install a crontab file for the current user.
Confirm the cron daemon is running.

lab.title: Archive, restore, and schedule
lab.scenario: Create a compressed archive of the fieldbook notes, prove it can be restored, then install a daily backup entry in the student crontab.

steps.text: Create a compressed archive of the notes directory under /home/student/lab.
steps.verify: The archive exists and is non-empty.

steps.text: List the archive contents before trusting it.
steps.verify: The listing includes notes/day1.txt and no absolute paths.

steps.text: Extract into a clean directory and compare the result.
steps.verify: The restored tree contains the same files as the source notes directory.

steps.text: Create a backup wrapper script that appends a timestamp to a log.
steps.cmd:
printf "#!/bin/bash
date >> /home/student/lab/archive/backup.log
tar -czf /home/student/lab/archive/fieldbook-notes.tar.gz -C /home/student/lab/fieldbook notes
" | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/fieldbook-backup && sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/fieldbook-backup
steps.verify: The script exists with execute permission and writes to the archive directory.

steps.text: Install a daily 02:00 crontab entry and inspect it.
steps.verify: crontab -l shows exactly the intended five-field entry.

steps.text: Confirm the cron daemon is running and compare with timer state.
steps.verify: crond is active and you can explain when you would choose a timer instead.

quiz.q: Which tar command lists a gzip archive without extracting it?
quiz.why: -t lists, -z handles gzip, and -f names the archive file.

quiz.q: In the cron entry 0 2 * * * /job, when does the job run?
options: At midnight on the second day of the month
quiz.why: The fields are minute, hour, day of month, month, and day of week: minute 0 of hour 2, every day.

quiz.q: Which is a strong reason to prefer a systemd timer for a system job?
options: Timers integrate with journald and unit dependencies
quiz.why: Timers give structured logging, dependency ordering, and Persistent catch-up behavior.
